segments.speaker: SPEAKER_0
segments.text: Today we are going to talk about hash tables, one of the most important data structures in computer science.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_0
segments.text: A hash table is a structure that maps keys to values using a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_0
segments.text: The average time complexity for lookups, insertions, and deletions is constant, or O of one.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_0
segments.text: When two keys hash to the same bucket we get what is called a collision and we need a strategy to resolve it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_0
segments.text: The two main collision resolution strategies are separate chaining and open addressing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_0
segments.text: Separate chaining stores a linked list at each bucket so multiple entries can share the same index.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_1
segments.text: Professor, what happens to performance when the load factor gets too high?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_0
segments.text: Great question. When the load factor exceeds a threshold we resize the table and rehash all the entries to keep operations fast.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_0
segments.text: A good hash function distributes keys uniformly to minimize clustering and keep collisions rare.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_0
segments.text: In summary, hash tables give you fast average-case access at the cost of worst-case guarantees and extra memory.
